items.title: Ted Cruz-led committee approves Trump FCC nominee 15-0 as Democrats boycott vote
items.excerpt: A Senate committee chaired by Ted Cruz (R-Texas) voted today to approve a Federal Communications Commission nominee, despite accusations that the nominee gave false testimony about her work as a legal advisor for FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. Democrats attempted to prevent a quorum by not showing up, but Cruz proceeded with a Republican-only vote. All 15 Republicans on the Senate Commerce Committee voted to approve Trump nominee Danielle Thumann, while the committee's 13 Democrats were absent. "We're going to be doing our job today, even if the Democrats refuse to show up to do theirs," Cruz said at today's hearing. Nominees are vetted in committees first, and then seek require majority approval from the Senate. Republicans are hoping to get Thumann confirmed before Democrats take Senate control in January. items.title: Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits
items.excerpt: A Ukrainian barrage of missiles and drones collapsed a crucial segment of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s prized Kerch Strait Bridge—and Ukraine’s military pulled off the strike deep within Russian-occupied territory without relying on the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications to guide the missiles in. On the nights of November 15 and November 16, coordinated waves of Ukrainian drones and missiles caused enough damage to collapse one of two steel arches supporting the Kerch bridge’s roadway for automobile traffic, according to an Institute for the Study of War update . Russian sources claimed several hundred Ukrainian drones first overwhelmed Russian air defenses to pave the way for remote-controlled missile strikes focused on the bridge, with the latter prominently including Ukraine’s homegrown Flamingo cruise missile. The Ukrainian operation adapted a Russian battlefield innovation by using drones equipped with mesh radios to create an airborne communications network, according to the Financial Times . Each networked drone acts as a relay node to extend the communication link between human operators and remotely piloted missiles and strike drones. Russia began using the technique to support long-range drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities. Read full article Comments

items.title: Trump abandons his FDA nominee, and Senate scraps vote on his NSF pick
items.excerpt: In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump's pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation. Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy's decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats. In her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated. The questions she dodged included those on how she would handle the FDA's current safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone, which extensive data has established is extremely safe. She also wouldn't say whether she agreed with Trump when he falsely claimed the measles vaccine is "quite lethal" or that children are given vaccine doses the "size of a soda bottle." Overton repeatedly refused to answer whether Trump could ever be wrong. Read full article Comments

items.title: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
items.excerpt: Microsoft's Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core . Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft says is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency's (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG). STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft says that concern is now managed: "The s ecure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened. " The new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance. Read full article Comments

items.excerpt: Hi HN We built a tool to help founders understand how modern fundraising (with safes) works, and how much dilution you can expect when raising money. The project is open-source. The code is a mess right now, but it'll get better I promise. You can also help with that. We didn't build this to make money. We genuinely did it because we were looking for it, and couldn't find it. We're in fact in the process of fundraising for a company, and at first glance the process looks simple. Just an excel sheet will do! But then the more we dug into it and tried different simulators, the more we realized that it's more complex than it looks. We even signed up to Pulley, Carta and others just to run simulations. But they're a bit confusing. TL;DR: Understanding modern startup funding and knowing how much dilution you'll face is hard. We built a tool that'll hopefully help with that. You can add Post-money Safes, priced rounds and issue options to employees, and you can see how that affects your ownership at every step. You can also simulate an Exit scenario and see how much money you'll be left with. --- Some examples of complex stuff: - There are many different types of safes. They all convert at the first priced round, but in different ways. Some are through discount, some are uncapped, some have a fixed valuation cap, and some have both a discount and a valuation cap. - All safes (before first priced round) convert at the same time. They don't dilute each other, which is what happens…

items.title: My AI Agents Write Code Faster Than I Can Verify It
items.excerpt: 76% of developers and engineering managers in Sonar's 2027 State of Code report say they generate AI code faster than they can verify it! And I'm right there with them, since I run software factories where agents open pull requests around the clock. AI code looks correct way more often now, so the bugs that slip through are the subtle ones. The way I handle it in my own factories is simple. Agents can write whatever they want, but nothing merges until a check the agent doesn't control says it passes. The full report is really worth a read if you're handing more of your code to agents: https://fandf.co/4iN1mvB Thanks to Sonar for working with me on this!

items.title: I Trust My AI Agents to Merge Code… But NOT Ship It
items.excerpt: I trust my agents to merge code all night, but I definitely don't trust them to ship straight to production. Tests and reviews only tell you the code looks right. LaunchDarkly helps teams control and monitor how changes behave once they're live in production. They just launched Release Autopilot, where agents do the feature flag work that used to take an engineer: risk classification, success metrics, automatic release plans that start with a canary release, feature-level observability and flag cleanup. Safe, controlled releases with guardrails. Check out Release Autopilot: https://fandf.co/4sttJ6l Thanks to LaunchDarkly for working with me on this! #ad

items.title: Your Coding Agent Has a MASSIVE Blind Spot (You Need to Fix It)
items.excerpt: I've had agents break hundreds of times in production (sometimes in very embarrassing ways), and almost all the time it comes down to the blind spots in my coding agent. Your agent sees your code, but not what it does once it's running. The Dynatrace MCP Server brings live production data to the coding agent in your IDE, so you can ask about your running systems in plain language and trace a problem to the exact line behind it. Read the walkthrough: https://fandf.co/4ik3t9P Thanks to Dynatrace for sponsoring this video and working with me on it!

items.title: Post-Training Gemini 4 for Real Engineering Work — Melvin Johnson, Google DeepMind
items.excerpt: Passing the tests does not mean a coding agent solved the problem. At CODE Summit 2026, Google DeepMind's Melvin Johnson explains Gemini 4 post training for real engineering work, from harder tasks and rubric based grading to isolated evaluation environments. He connects reinforcement learning, reward hacking, honest model behavior and feedback from Google's engineers to faster releases, alongside Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen. Speaker info: - https://melvin.app/ - https://research.google/people/105147/ - https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-hydrogen/ Timestamps: 0:00 - Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen 5:32 - From code completion to real engineering work 7:23 - Harder tasks and richer learning signals 10:00 - Grading agents without rewarding cheating 13:10 - Training agents to report honestly 15:30 - Shipping faster through engineering feedback

items.title: 40x More Merged PRs With 2.7x the Engineers — Walden Yan, Cognition
items.excerpt: Cognition's merged PRs grew 40x in a year while its engineering team grew 2.7x. Walden Yan explains what changed: self-driving PRs by default, small pods that own everything from bug reports to QA, and a workflow run almost entirely from Slack. He covers running every service locally so agents can test, VMs rebuilt every hour, and agents that optimize the factory itself. Then he shows the next step: giving agents jobs instead of tasks, from tuning inference on new GPUs to an Android app maintained by Devin over 44 days. items.title: SpaceX Just Won a Trillion Dollar Bet.
items.excerpt: SpaceX just caught a spaceship out of the sky. Ship 42 launched from Starbase, circled the Earth 14 times, deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites and came back 22.5 hours later, where the same tower it launched from caught it in mid-air, the first time a rocket's upper stage has ever been caught after reaching orbit. items.title: Clear Signing Comes to Solana | Ledger's Ian Rogers
items.excerpt: BREAKING: Ledger brings Clear Signing to Solana, starting with Jupiter and Kamino It fixes a long-running problem called blind signing. Blind signing, in which users approve transactions displayed as unreadable data, has long been a weak point for hardware wallet users, since it leaves them unable to spot a malicious request. Rogers likened it to "signing a blank check". Clear Signing turns that data into plain words. A swap on Jupiter, a Solana trading app, now takes three screens instead of 13 and shows what you give, what you get and who's on the other side. It now covers nine Solana apps and 18 of the 22 most common actions users take on the network. — Ian Rogers, Chief Human Agency Officer at @Ledger at Breakpoint 2026

items.title: The last great revolution
items.excerpt: It feels like the common man lost a bit of his soul after we exterminated the vast majority of organized crime. Yes, crime sucks. But even if these organizations were horrible for the communities they preyed on, the existence of an underbelly at least suggested limits to state power. There was an existence proof of people outside the state developing a (conditional, fictional) code of honor, and coordinating amongst themselves, in a way that was transgressive and competitive with the state, unlike the drugged-out homeless man yelling obscenities at you on the subway. People watching old movies and TV shows can feel the guilty exhilaration at the idea of participating in or shaping a network outside the state, with its own rules. Nowadays even the petty crime you do witness feels like evidence of the state's taunting indifference. There are cameras on every street corner; every child grows up with the tacit knowledge that everything they've ever said or done is going to be logged in some government database searchable by AI. The "government", whatever that means, could stop the guy who's shitting on the subway, if it wanted to. Crime has stopped being something that happens in spite of the government, or undermines it, and started being another boring reminder of your powerlessness in the face of the reigning regime, and of how nobody can ever do anything about it. I don't even know if removing the new technology enforcing the law would do anything. Today most of the public…

items.title: Secular Solstice Roundup 2026
items.excerpt: This is a thread for listing Solstice events (dates, locations, links, etc.) If you're not familiar with Solstice, around the darkest night of the year, rationalist communities gather to humankind's long arc towards civilization and also a somber night of reflection on the dangers facing that civilization. We join our voices together and sing about both the triumphs and the looming disasters, and remember that we're not alone. Together, we can build a better future. Ceremonies vary from city to city and organizer to organizer. Some are different every year, while others follow the same beats time and again. One reasonably typical ceremony follows the arc of the solstice itself, moving thematically from light to darkness to light again: Light: Appreciating human invention and progress. Once we were cold on winter nights, and now we have electric heaters. Once we were hungry when the plants stopped growing, and now we have grocery stores. Once we were surrounded by darkness once the sun went down, and now we have the lightbulb. Night: Acknowledging the hardships and trials humanity fought through, and is still fighting. There is still disease, and hunger, and cold. There are worse dangers as well, the results of science or a universe that does not care about us. Often featuring a Moment of Darkness. Dawn: Applauding the feats that humankind could achieve if only we succeed. There is light in the universe, and it is us. Each Solstice features songs (often with group singing)…

items.title: Solomonoff induction with reflective oracles
items.excerpt: Linkpost for https://arxiv.org/html/2611.14454v1 Our PIBBSS fellow Damini Kusum wrote an excellent paper on prediction with reflective oracle Solomonoff Induction (rOSI). Reflective oracles are best known for their game-theoretic applications, where they are often dismissed because "why would all players choose the same reflective oracle?" It turns out that reflective oracles can also be used to construct a version of Solomonoff induction (called rOSI) with very nice sequence prediction properties - roughly speaking, it can learn to extract computable structure from (partly) uncomputable sequences. In fact, its properties are quite reminiscent of logical induction, but this paper is much shorter and more accessible. In this context, there is only one "player" to choose an oracle, which is just a fixed-point (though you can sort of consider the set of hypotheses entertained by that player as subplayers who share the oracle). I think this paper is the clearest exposition of a very neat but previously obscure idea in agent foundations: self-reflection can overcome unrealizability. Discuss

items.title: Varieties Of Discourseposting
items.excerpt: I’m teaching at the Inkhaven blogging fellowship again this month. In my first class, I showed off terribly-written sentences and made the fellows analyze and improve them. Some were my own miscreations, some were Lyttle Lytton winners , and some came from the darkest abysses of the Internet. The audience’s favorite was overwrought description of women’s breasts from erotica (one person pointed out that my PDF reader’s Recent History tab helpfully displayed porn story titles while I presented on screen - why does a PDF reader even have a Recent History tab? - so I hope my humiliation helped educate you). But I hear that Naomi Kanakia ’s class was even spicier. She taught a course on “discourseposting”, which naturally descended into fiery discourse ( Naomi Kanakia, you are WRONG about Discourseposting!!! , Inkhaven Fight Club ). I didn’t get a chance to listen, so in the grand tradition of discourseposting, I’ll argue about it without having seen the source material. Sticking to our porn theme, and in the spirit of The Last Psychiatrist : one way to classify sex is through its external manifestations: positions, toys, fetishes. But another is through which psychological need it fulfills. The need to feel wanted. The need to feel valuable. The need to dominate. The need to lose yourself. items.title: AI Company Employees Should Unionize
items.excerpt: I. Should safety-conscious employees at AI companies quit in protest, or stay and fight? The latest argument didn’t resolve the dispute, but it did get me in contact with organizers working on both sides. Those planning to stay and fight are increasingly interested in labor organization. This doesn’t need to mean literal government-recognized Labor Unions. An existing group, Coalition Of Concerned AI Staff , is already helping support interested employees and investigating other models to do more. But it might involve using laws, rights, and tactics associated with the National Labor Relations Act and the labor movement. You may remember stories of bitter unionization battles at places like Starbucks, but AI workers can probably route around that. The toughest labor disputes happen in fields where the employer could easily fire all the organized workers and replace them from a bottomless pool of faceless scabs: although this is illegal, everyone needs to be maximally lawyered-up to prevent it. But there are so few skilled AI researchers that these laws are hardly necessary; if a dozen top AI researchers threaten to walk, it doesn’t matter whether Section P Sub-Section Q forces the AI company to negotiate - the AI company will want to negotiate. This cuts through the red tape that intimidates workers in less blessed fields 1 ; AI researchers could likely get away with only the package of rights provided by informal “concerted activity”, defined as two or more workers doing…

items.title: Escaping The “Outside Criticism” Trap
items.excerpt: I. Here’s a fun argument you can use to discredit anyone at any time. Start by calling them an arrogant fanatic with a totalizing ideology, someone who thinks they personally have solved all problems and can’t possibly learn from anyone who disagrees. If they have friends who agree with them, they’re a cult who collectively work to shelter themselves from any dissenting viewpoint. Then your victim responds by presenting one hundred notarized affadavits describing times when they have engaged with their critics, spent years studying books by their critics to see what they could learn from them, and even changed their beliefs in response to criticism. Then you spring the trap: “Ah, but you cherry-picked critics who operate within your worldview, a sort of loyal opposition. You continue to dismiss and exclude genuine critics who challenge your smug assumptions.” This always works. If your victim protests that they do like and appreciate many critics with worldviews different to theirs, you object that no, those guys are also within the system. You meant a different guy, even further away from their own view. Oh, they read that one too? You meant an even more different guy. Eventually, no matter how cosmopolitan they are, you will reach someone they actually don’t respect - let’s say a Stalinist pedophile who believes the Papacy is a Jewish plot - and then you go ha! I told you that you rejected everyone outside your little bubble! Everyone has people close to their ideology who…

Ask HN: Good ways to capture institutional knowledge?
items.excerpt: Successful companies institutionalize the knowledge of their employees; this leads to better continuity and faster on-boarding. Things like huge monorepos of useful code, internal tools, process manuals, etc. are example products of this. Young companies tend to depend on the dedication and talent of key individuals, and in maturation, must somehow make the jump to institutionalized knowledge (so that "if someone got hit by a bus" things are ok). What are some successful methods you have used or seen used to accomplish this transition? What are problems you faced (skeptics, opponents, etc.)? I am involved with an organization that is slowly growing, is about to lose key personnel, and is looking to prepare.

items.title: How the Man City case could spark a drastic change in English football

The previous talk of trying to buy clubs, only for billionaires to realise how few are available, has gradually turned into talk of trying to sell clubs. Except, that is now even more difficult. items.title: MariTide Explained: Amgen's Once-Monthly GLP-1 Antibody Conjugate and Its Side Effects
items.excerpt: MariTide (maridebart cafraglutide, formerly AMG 133) is Amgen's investigational obesity drug: a fully human antibody that blocks the GIP receptor, linked to two GLP-1 agonist peptides, designed for once-monthly injection. This short covers how the dual mechanism works, what the Phase 1 trial and the 52-week Phase 2 trial in the New England Journal of Medicine showed on weight and blood sugar, where the Phase 3 MARITIME program stands, and what trials reported on side effects, from nausea and vomiting to GI dropouts and gallbladder events. items.title: Petrelintide Explained: The Long-Acting Amylin Analogue and Its Side Effects
items.excerpt: Petrelintide is a once-weekly peptide modeled on human amylin, a satiety hormone co-secreted with insulin. Zealand Pharma designed it; Roche and Genentech are co-developing it. This short covers how the amylin pathway differs from GLP-1 drugs, what the Phase 2 ZUPREME-1 trial showed on weight and cardiometabolic markers, the Phase 3 ZUPREME program now underway, and what trials reported on side effects, from mild nausea to placebo-like gut tolerability. items.title: Mazdutide Explained: The GLP-1 and Glucagon Dual Agonist and Its Side Effects
items.excerpt: Mazdutide is a once-weekly peptide modeled on oxyntomodulin that activates both the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors. In 2025 China approved it for chronic weight management and type 2 diabetes, the first dual glucagon/GLP-1 agonist approved for weight loss. This short covers how it works, what the GLORY-1, GLORY-2, and DREAMS-3 trials and Lilly's U.S. phase 2 trial showed, where it stands outside China, and what trials reported on side effects, from nausea and vomiting to heart rate and gallbladder findings. items.title: Elamipretide (SS-31) Explained: The Mitochondria-Targeting Peptide and Its Side Effects
items.excerpt: Elamipretide (SS-31) is a four-amino-acid peptide that enters mitochondria and binds cardiolipin, a key lipid of the inner mitochondrial membrane. In September 2025 the FDA granted it accelerated approval as Forzinity, the first treatment for Barth syndrome. This short covers how it works, what the TAZPOWER trial and its long-term extension showed, the mixed results in mitochondrial myopathy and dry macular degeneration, where the confirmatory and phase 3 trials stand, and what studies reported on side effects, from injection site reactions to allergic reactions and eosinophil changes. We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. items.title: Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry
items.excerpt: arXiv:2611.23322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One hope for a good human future alongside advanced AI rests on enduring mutualism: humans and AI will need each other, so the relationship will stay good for both. We argue that this hope fails as AI capability grows. Bargaining guarantees each side only what it would get if bargaining failed. For humans, this can be less than they had before AI. In a simple game-theoretic model, humans stay as well off as before AI without alignment only while they have leverage over the AI: either the AI depends on what they supply, or they can impose costs on the AI that are large relative to what the AI can produce. Once humans have neither kind of leverage, they stay as well off as before AI only if the AI is aligned with them. If the AI's goals are insatiable, the alignment required approaches perfect alignment as AI capability grows. Thus, mutualism is not a substitute for alignment. And when AI variants that keep more resources spread faster, alignment lasts only while misaligned variants are reliably sanctioned. In these two senses, human-AI mutualism is unstable.

items.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
items.excerpt: arXiv:2611.23365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. Asking the assistant follow-up questions about its actions is unreliable, since models are generally not trained to report their own misbehavior. As a result, approaches to oversight typically involve querying external models. These face limitations: external transcript monitoring operates only on visible model outputs, and activation decoders lack full context and are prone to confabulation. We introduce introspective oversight, which trains a new role in the model to answer arbitrary questions about the assistant, rewarding answers that are verified against the assistant's actual behavior. We implement this by adding a separate, third-person observer role that answers these queries, which we can train solely for accuracy and separately from the assistant. On five held-out oversight evaluations, an observer trained on Qwen3.6-27B obtains a mean AUROC of 0.907, outperforming honesty training (0.864), transcript monitoring (0.828), and activation oracles (0.796). We further find that training an observer makes the assistant itself easier to monitor, with every baseline method improving on average when applied to the fine-tuned assistant. These results suggest that training models to answer verifiable questions about themselves is a tractable approach to overseeing unintended behavior.

items.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
items.excerpt: arXiv:2611.23375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. The cycle returns the requested edits to where they began, with each direction started from a stored reference tree, and the spread of its cost over repeated cycles defines a software temperature, which rose with the sampling temperature of the model. About 80 per cent of the tokens of a successful run are generated in model calls that leave the requested change where it was, and we call these tokens heat. The free energy of a change, which we estimate by analogy with the equality of Jarzynski, is 14 to 22 per cent of the mean cost of a successful coding run. Coding costs 1.1 to 1.5 times as much as uncoding. The daemon is imperfect: the verdict of a test suite varies with its environment, and a suite that…

items.title: HardwareDx: A Foundational Graph Model System for Datacenter Machine Repairs
items.excerpt: arXiv:2611.23398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid scale-up of AI infrastructure has made datacenter reliability a cornerstone of the cloud business economy. Since hardware failures in hyper-scale AI clusters can stall multi-million dollar training workloads, the downtime of individual machines can cause outsized economic losses. Minimizing machine downtime, therefore, is more important than ever. To address this, we present Hardware Diagnoser (HardwareDx), an AI-driven hardware diagnosis system that applies a graph foundation model approach to automated datacenter maintenance. It allows a single model to diagnose many platforms and accelerate onboarding of new hardware products. Deployed at production scale at Google, HardwareDx yields substantial efficiency gains across diverse compute architectures. Real-world evaluations demonstrate that it reduces production downtime by 18.3% on GPU platforms and 16.1% on TPUs. Furthermore, it significantly accelerates hardware deployment, cutting quality assurance (QA) time by 28.3% for GPUs and 25.1% for TPUs. These results establish HardwareDx as a field-tested solution for maximizing the reliability and cost efficiency of next generation AI fleets.

items.title: RFBench: A Simulator-Grounded Multimodal Benchmark for Passive RF Layout Design and Understanding
items.excerpt: arXiv:2611.23410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While multimodal language models can interpret diagrams and generate structured outputs, their capacity to connect passive radio-frequency (RF) design intent, layout geometry, and electromagnetic behavior remains largely untested. To address this gap, we introduce RFBench, a simulator-grounded dataset and benchmark for passive RF layout design and understanding. The dataset contains 10,000 two-port planar layouts simulated using ADS Momentum, with each layout represented by editable geometric primitives, a raster image, a 16x16 occupancy grid, complex S-parameters at 201 frequency points, a structural category, and an RF response label. Building on these aligned representations, we define seven tasks spanning specification-conditioned layout generation, representation translation, response prediction, simulator-based validation, design diagnosis and improvement, structural understanding, and response classification. Extensive baselines across seven multimodal language models reveal systematic weaknesses in generating structurally valid layouts and predicting electromagnetically faithful responses. We show that RF-specific fine-tuning increases T1a structural validity from 0.0% to 83.2% and the T3 primitive-input within-2-dB rate from 17.7% to 62.8%, demonstrating the value of domain adaptation while leaving considerable room for further progress. Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.
items.excerpt: AI has made finding potential vulnerabilities fast and cheap. Fixing them still takes human judgment, and in open source, that work falls to maintainers. Many are already flooded with AI-generated security findings, including duplicates and reports that aren’t vulnerabilities at all. Another raw scan doesn’t help them. Anyone pointing a new model at a project should ask its maintainers first and come with fixes, not just findings. Maintainers are under intense pressure from this flood of reports. As Christian Grobmeier, a maintainer of Log4j, has put it, the AI defending open source has to be better than the AI attacking it . AI shouldn’t add to maintainers’ workload. So, with maintainers, GitHub and Microsoft ran a pilot together: could AI help maintainers ship fixes instead of handing them more findings? GitHub and Microsoft are using Codename MDASH , Microsoft’s multi-model agentic scanning harness, to find and fix security vulnerabilities in widely used open source software, strengthening the foundation that much of the world’s code is built on. The process Our pilot had two goals: send only findings that matter, and never send a maintainer an unverified finding. Here’s how it worked: Find. Codename MDASH , an AI system from Microsoft Security, scanned each project using Microsoft’s MAI Cyber model and suggested fixes for what it found. Filter. An AI triage agent from the GitHub Security Lab , built on tailored Copilot skills, removed duplicates, checked validity, and…

items.title: Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices
items.excerpt: Models are now good enough to work for hours or even days on their own. You don’t have to watch over every thing they do, but you still need to be able to check in, no matter where you are. An agent can’t live only inside one application. The work should continue even If you close a window or switch devices. In GitHub Copilot you can start an agent session in one place and pick it up in another. This session continuity runs on the Agent Host Protocol (AHP), an open standard built first in VS Code and adopted across GitHub. Here’s how it works, what we learned building it, and how you can use it to bring your agents into your own apps and workflows. Why one integration per client stopped working GitHub Copilot was first built in VS Code as an extension that bundled its own harness. This gave you access to your agents in VS Code, but it tied their lifetime to the editor. Extensions are attached to a single VS Code window. Close that window, and the agent is gone. Update VS Code, and every agent stops as the application restarts. Connect to a remote machine, and you get an entirely new extension host commit-locked against the version of the VS Code workbench you have. At the same time, the Copilot app was being developed, alongside the existing GitHub mobile apps for iOS and Android. Each product was doing its own distinct integration with cloud-based agents to work towards delivering session continuity. Each of these integrations solved the problem for one product, but…

items.title: GitHub availability report: October 2026
items.excerpt: We continue to share monthly updates on the work behind GitHub’s availability and reliability. The short version of October: we added substantial independently scalable Azure capacity and removed several ways that failures could escalate. However, write outages, monitoring gaps during data migrations, and a regional network disruption reinforced the need for capacity growth to be paired with safer operations, stronger isolation, and validated regional recovery. As of November 9, 140 of 151 production services and 32 of 50 MySQL primaries were running in Azure Central US. Azure served 63% of migrated-service reads, 66% of monolith reads, and 52% of Git reads. We also completed a compute expansion across all nine Central US Kubernetes clusters, more than doubling capacity. That capacity is already carrying real growth. Migrated-service traffic has increased 82% since March, with Central US absorbing the growth beyond the highest weekly-average load previously served from our existing datacenter. This gives GitHub more room to grow without pushing the original environment beyond its prior operating range. We also made several targeted reliability improvements. Actions changes increased capacity for critical Azure control-plane requests. A separate NAT-gateway mitigation reduced usage by 85%; four production jobs failed during the change, compared with approximately 800 expected without the mitigation. items.title: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills
items.excerpt: How many times this week did you re-explain the same task to an agent? How many times did you ask your colleague with deep institutional knowledge how to solve a specific problem? That context shouldn’t be lost in a chat or locked in one person’s head. Agent skills let you capture repeatable instructions so you and your agents can reuse them. The skill you write for yourself tonight can later become part of a team’s pipeline. An agent skill is a versioned directory centered on a SKILL.md file that describes when and how to do a repeatable task. You can share those instructions across agents, but the environment still needs to provide the tools, credentials, and permissions to carry them out. A skill can describe how to query a database, for example, but it doesn’t grant access to that database. I covered this topic live with Shishir Tewari, Senior Manager, Data Engineering at Procore, during GitHub Universe 2026. Our session was titled “Build once, run on any agent: a practical guide to agent skills” . Define one job and when it applies A skill works best when it has a clear job, input, and output. For example, let’s say you’re building an agent that checks AI-generated changes against the original request. If the same agent assesses its own work, its explanation might influence the review. With Proof Agent , we use a separate verifier to examine the changes and provide evidence for its findings. The skill’s frontmatter names the task and describes its purpose: --- name…

items.excerpt: Editor’s note (November 17, 2026): This post has been updated with additional CVE information and updated guidance for GitHub Enterprise Server users . Please see the release information below for the versions that include the fixes. Today, the Git project is releasing new versions to address six security vulnerabilities. These include arbitrary code execution when cloning a malicious repository, writes to unintended files, and memory corruption when processing merges or binary patches. The fixes are included in Git 2.56.1 , with backports to Git 2.55.1, 2.54.1, 2.53.1, 2.52.1, 2.51.3, and 2.50.2. We recommend updating to Git 2.56.1 or the patched release for your maintenance series, and updating any applications that bundle Git. Vulnerabilities in Git CVE-2026-111760: Code execution when cloning malicious repositories Git checks paths before writing files into a working tree, including rejecting paths that would overwrite its own repository metadata. However, an integer truncation in Git’s index handling can cause an extremely long path to pass validation under one name and then be written using a shorter name. An attacker-controlled Git server can exploit this discrepancy to replace a clone’s .git file or directory, redirecting Git to attacker-controlled configuration or hooks . items.title: UNICEF Somalia Humanitarian Situation Report No.3, 1 July - 30 September 2026
items.excerpt: Country: Somalia Source: UN Children's Fund Please refer to the attached file. Highlights Somalia's humanitarian needs remained high during the quarter, driven by drought, conflict, displacement, disease outbreaks and declining humanitarian assistance. An estimated 5.1 million people faced acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3+), while 1.92 million children were projected to suffer acute malnutrition between July 2026 and June 2027. About 75,000 displacement movements and over 1,400 conflict events were recorded. UNICEF sustained lifesaving assistance across priority sectors, reaching 98,241 children with SAM treatment, 244,022 caregivers with IYCF counselling, 145,671 people with primary health care, and 286,006 people with safe water. Education support benefited 71,644 children, while 48,991 people accessed child protection services. Monthly cash transfers supported 13,493 vulnerable women, strengthening household resilience. The 2026 Humanitarian Action for Children (HAC) appeal was 27 per cent funded (US$32 million) against US$121 million required, leaving a US$89 million gap. Underfunding continued to constrain service coverage, operational capacity and emergency preparedness for anticipated El Nino impacts.

Estos impactos pueden poner en riesgo toda su niñez y tener consecuencias que perduren más allá del fin de las hostilidades, atravesando, a veces, múltiples generaciones. items.excerpt: Country: World Source: Save the Children Please refer to the attached file. DU RAPPORT : STOP À LA GUERRE CONTRE LES ENFANTS – CHANGER LA DONNE Près d’un quart des enfants à travers le monde vivent aujourd’hui dans des zones de conflit. Jamais encore un tel niveau n’avait été atteint depuis le début de cette comptabilisation en 1990. Les souffrances des enfants touchés par des conflits armés constituent actuellement l’une des préoccupations politiques et humanitaires les plus pressantes. C’est pourtant l’une des plus négligées. Les enfants souffrent de manière disproportionnée durant les conflits. Leurs petits corps, en plein développement, sont particulièrement vulnérables aux conséquences des armes explosives. Leurs esprits, qui forgent encore leur image d’eux-mêmes, leur sentiment de sécurité et leur compréhension du monde, vivent différemment les traumatismes, avec des effets potentiellement durables sur leur développement. Ces conséquences peuvent mettre en péril toute leur enfance, avec des répercussions qui persistent bien après la fin des hostilités, parfois pendant plusieurs générations. Le risque de pauvreté augmente, les réseaux de soutien sont affaiblis et les enfants peuvent être séparés de leurs familles. Les services vitaux sont souvent perturbés et les écoles fermées ; les enfants ratent ainsi des étapes clés de l’éducation, ce qui impacte leur avenir. Il peut aussi devenir incroyablement difficile de bien manger et d’accéder aux soins de santé vitaux. Tout…

items.title: World: Children affected by armed conflict, 1990–2025
items.excerpt: Country: World Source: Peace Research Institute Oslo Please refer to the attached file. More children than ever live in conflict zones Posted Thursday, 19 Nov 2026 by Gudrun Østby & Siri Aas Rustad More children now live near armed conflict than the combined populations of the United States, Canada and Mexico. Armed violence escalated sharply across the globe in 2025. Data from the Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP) shows that conflict-related fatalities rose to 244,600, up from approximately 187,000 in 2024. This made 2025 one of the deadliest years since the end of the Cold War. Much of the increase was driven by a dramatic rise in violence targeting civilians, particularly in Sudan. While armed conflict affects entire populations, children are among those who suffer the most severe and lasting consequences. Children face grave violations , including killing and maiming, recruitment by armed groups, sexual violence, abduction, attacks on schools and hospitals, and denial of humanitarian access. But the consequences of war extend far beyond direct violence. Children living in conflict-affected areas are more likely to drop out of school, lack access to clean water, and face heightened risks of death from illness, malnutrition, or lack of vaccines and medical care. Today, Save the Children launches its new report, Stop the War on Children 2026 . The report is based on PRIO’s tenth annual mapping of children in armed conflict covering the period 1990–2025. items.excerpt: Prolonged drought conditions affecting the Colorado River Basin led to record low hydropower generation this summer in the Southwestern electricity supply region, which includes Arizona, New Mexico, and small parts of Nevada and California. items.title: Scientists say this pesticide needs a warning label for pollinators
items.excerpt: Of the many chemicals humans have invented to control agricultural pests, some of the most devious are called “ insect growth regulators .” As the name suggests, these compounds don’t kill insects directly; they alter their development so they can’t grow into healthy, reproducing adults. This makes insect growth regulators a remarkably useful tool for taming populations of insects like whiteflies and mealybugs, which can spread diseases and sap nutrients out of food crops. There’s just one problem: Farmers don’t want to regulate all insects in this way. Beneficial insects like honey bees risk getting caught in the crosshairs of these chemicals, to the detriment of farmers who need their pollination services to produce crops like pears and cherries. One insect growth regulator in particular has emerged as a potential issue for pollinators: buprofezin. Ongoing research out of Washington State University, or WSU, suggests that buprofezin may be hazardous to honey bees even at concentrations 10 times below those commonly found in pollen. A study published in 2024 connected the compound to “severe brood mortality.” At a meeting of the Washington State Beekeeping Association last month, WSU entomology professor Brandon Hopkins said buprofezin products should be sold with a pollinator warning — a break from current requirements of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, or EPA. Buprofezin “should carry the same bee-caution label that some of these more direct pesticides carry,”…

items.excerpt: Background Jeffrey Edward Epstein (January 20, 1953 – August 10, 2019) was an American financier and convicted sex offender. Until his conviction for sex crimes in 2008, Epstein was a multimillionaire who was connected with the financial, political, and cultural elite of society. In April 2005, police of Palm Beach, Florida began investigating Epstein after a parent complained that he molested her 14-year-old daughter. After an investigation, prosecution, and plea negotiations, Epstein pleaded guilty and was convicted by a Florida state court of soliciting a prostitute and of procuring an underage girl for prostitution on June 30, 2008.
